question: does richer OFFLINE partitioning (SKN) allow simpler STRUCT-only ONLINE serving (E3) to match the shipped SK+FULL_C online mechanism (E2)?
NOTE: Accuracy ties within noise (same as webqsp), but the COST direction is OPPOSITE of webqsp's finding: on hotpot SKN's STRUCT-only online path is somewhat MORE expensive than SK's shipped FULL_C path (~48% higher latency, slightly more candidates), not cheaper. hotpot's SKN hypergraph carries far more NER-driven structure (raw NER mentions 4.34M vs webqsp's 1.22M) which likely explains why STRUCT-only no longer shrinks the online candidate set here. Measured on a shared, resource-constrained local machine over a multi-hour run -- treat magnitude as directional, but the SIGN FLIP vs webqsp (cheaper there, costlier here) is a real cross-corpus finding, not just noise: a uniform 'always serve STRUCT-only under SKN' policy is NOT free everywhere.
